title: Recent three-month SST change gave no clear added May Nino 3.4 forecast gain in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether recent sea surface temperature change improves direct three-month Nino 3.4 forecasts beyond current level. We used a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 record and expanding fits for target years 1981-2025. Adding the preceding three-month change reduced May mean squared error by 1.31%. Conditional 95% five-year block limits were -20.58% to 22.06%. May minus November percentage reduction was 9.01 points, with limits -12.73 to 27.79. Thus the added May gain and its seasonal contrast were uncertain. Shorter training, one-month change, a six-month lead and test halves also gave uncertain May gains. History helped some other seasons and leads in marginal checks. This is a scoped forecast benchmark, not a new method or a physical explanation of the spring barrier. Revised data, 45 years, fixed linear models and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Numerical inputs, provenance, all forecasts, code, a figure and a separate scalar audit are included.

display.caption: Three-month forecasts in 1981-2025. Error reductions have marginal conditional 95% five-year block limits. May is primary; November is the fixed comparison.
